parts.label: a
parts.technique: Impulse = change in momentum for a particle
parts.reason: No statement in the current 9MA0 spec covers momentum or impulse (M6-M9 sections given are only quantities/units, kinematics, forces/Newton's laws, and moments; momentum/impulse is absent entirely).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Conservation of linear momentum in a collision
parts.reason: Conservation of momentum (CLM) is not covered by any listed statement; no section on momentum/impulse exists in the given spec content.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: suvat constant acceleration formula
parts.reason: M7.3 covers constant acceleration formulae for straight-line motion; finding acceleration from s, u, t is standard.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: suvat to find velocity
parts.reason: M7.3 covers use of constant acceleration formulae to find speed.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Motion under gravity, constant acceleration formulae
parts.reason: M7.3/M8.3 cover motion under gravity with constant g; finding height after burnout uses suvat with g.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sketching speed-time graph
parts.reason: M7.2 explicitly covers interpreting/using velocity-time graphs including gradient and area, which includes sketching such graphs from given motion description.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Area under speed-time graph to find distance/time
parts.reason: M7.2 covers area under velocity-time graph representing distance; used here to find total time via given distance.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Area under graph / suvat to find unknown speed V
parts.reason: Combination of M7.2 (area under graph) and M7.3 (constant acceleration formulae) used to solve for V given total distance.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Resolving forces parallel to inclined plane, equilibrium
parts.reason: M8.4 guidance explicitly extends equilibrium of forces to inclined-plane problems requiring resolution of forces; this is exactly such a case.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Resolving forces perpendicular to plane to find normal reaction
parts.reason: Same inclined plane equilibrium context, covered by M8.4 guidance (resolving forces, inclined plane).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Newton's second law on inclined plane with resolved forces
parts.reason: M8.2 guidance explicitly extends Newton's second law to situations requiring resolving forces, e.g. a particle on an inclined plane.

parts.label: (a)(i)(ii)
parts.technique: Moments of a uniform rod, equilibrium
parts.reason: M9.1 covers moments in simple static contexts including rigid body/rod equilibrium with two supports.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Moments with variable position of load
parts.reason: M9.1 covers moments problems; expressing tension in terms of y is standard moments application.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Solving inequality from moments equation
parts.reason: Follows directly from part (b)'s in-spec moments expression, solved via linear inequality (P2.5) applied in mechanics context; both underlying techniques are in spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Magnitude of a velocity vector (speed)
parts.reason: M7.3 extends kinematics to 2D using vectors; finding speed as magnitude of velocity vector uses P10.2 magnitude of a vector, both in spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Direction of vector as bearing
parts.reason: M7.3 covers 2D vector kinematics; direction/bearing calculations are standard ordinary vector work (in spec per vector guidance), not excluded (no dot product/skew line concept involved).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Position vector with constant velocity, solving for unknown velocity components
parts.reason: M7.3 covers suvat/position vector formulae in 2D vector form (r=ut+...); finding u,v from position vector conditions is standard vector kinematics.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Vector kinematics to find time when displacement satisfies a direction condition
parts.reason: Continues the in-spec vector kinematics method (M7.3), using position vector components; no excluded concept (e.g., skew lines) is required.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Newton's second law for connected particles via pulley
parts.reason: M8.4 guidance explicitly covers problems involving smooth pulleys and connected particles.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Newton's second law with friction on connected particle system
parts.reason: M8.6 covers the F ≤ μR model and motion of a body on a rough surface, combined with M8.4 connected particles/pulleys.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: suvat before/after event, then decelerating motion with friction
parts.reason: Uses M7.3 constant acceleration formulae and M8.6 friction deceleration once B lands; entirely in-spec kinematics/forces methods.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Modelling assumption: light string means equal tension throughout
parts.reason: This is a basic modelling assumption within the Forces and Newton's laws context (tension concept from M8.1, connected particles M8.4); no excluded concept involved.
